questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The German marked is of great importance to Denmark and knowledge to the German Legal system and skills in the language is a great advantage.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The Copenhagen University delivered a very nice overview of the requirements and the deadline. However the material from Humboldt was all written in German in a very high level which did make the process a bit complicated and confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Humboldt had an exchange office where you could receive guidance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were certain courses which were possible to apply and receive the material but where the administration apparently didn't approve that Erasmus students could attend. This was very confusing since the professors etc. would tell you that you could attend the course but then you would receive a denial from the administation several weeks after the beginning of thee course,

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was normal

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As written above all the material regarding thee course registration etc. were in German and was complicated so the registration process was a bit confusing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Google Translate

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not so succesfull. As written above I was able to successfully apply for courses through the university's internet portal but then later was told by the administration that I wasn't allowed to attend to those courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Really take your time making sure that the administration approves it. It dosen't matter that you successfully have applied for the course hrough the university's internet portal or receive the professor's acceptance.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more the professors talking and the students listning compared to KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them but there is a big difference in the teaching style from german professors and the international professors. Both of them are good and recommendable so therefore I would suggeest that you try them both.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Germany introduced a summer national travel discount where you could get a ticket of the use of all public transports the whole summer for 9 euro only. That obvious saved some money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were sports activities and cultural activities available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Kreuzberg or Neukölln when partying and try visit the techno clubs even though you are not the typical type.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: VIsit some of the other germans cities.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very nice. Germans in Berlin are very polite and cool.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open. The German (especially the youth) are very polite and cool.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None I have only positive things to say.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The subculture and techno environment in Berlin even though I'm not the stereotypical type. I know many of the others were not as well but they were all impressed. I my advise would be to drop your prejudices (if you have any) and be open minded.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Try your best to speak and learn german. Even of you are terrible people really support you and appreciate you trying. And you will improve very fast if you just are trying.  

2) Explore thee subculture of Berlin 

3) Enjoy one the greatest cities in Europe

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to spend the summer in Berlin. I have heard that Berlin can be a bit rough during the winter.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Knowledge to german (language and professional knowledge)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Remembering to study since you are having so much fun.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
